Title: Bhai Tera Star Hai Movie Review: Raghav Juyal leads a comedy where the jokes need their own rescue mission
# Bhai Tera Star Hai Movie Review: Raghav Juyal leads a comedy where the jokes need their own rescue mission. ## ‘Bhai Tera Star Hai’ has a promising one-night comedy setup but gets trapped in its own web of confusion. Raghav Juyal brings energy, but weak writing ensures the laughs never truly arrive. Raghav Juyal stars in Bhai Tera Star Hai. * 'Bhai Tera Star Hai' released on July 30. * Stars Raghav Juyal, Sanjay Kapoor. ‘Bhai Tera Star Hai,’ directed by Vivek B Agrawal, released in theatres on 30 July and stars Raghav Juyal, Niki Walia, Sanjay Kapoor, Niharika NM, and Parvathy Omanakuttan. ‘Bhai Tera Star Hai’ is a comedy that unfolds over one chaotic night in London. It follows a young man who is convinced that becoming a superstar is only a matter of time until a cricket bet turns his life upside down. The film has a decent setup and enough ingredients for a fun entertainer, but it never figures out how to make the most of them. Ajay Singh (Raghav Juyal) is a struggling actor in London who is convinced that he is destined to become Bollywood’s next superstar. His dreams hit a roadblock when he loses money in a cricket bet and finds himself owing £10,000 to Fatty (Sanjay Kapoor). The characters keep creating new problems so quickly that even the audience starts wondering if there is a reward for the person who can create the biggest mess. Watching ‘Bhai Tera Star Hai’ gives a sense that the writers were more focussed on creating chaos than crafting comedy. A one-night comedy driven by misunderstandings can be great fun, but the screenplay keeps introducing new characters and side tracks without giving any of them enough purpose. Raghav Juyal gives the film plenty of energy and remains committed even when the screenplay lets him down. Raghav Juyal has the natural ability to carry a comedy, but this film does not give him the material needed to showcase that talent fully.
